title: Mini lab docket — quant & prompt quickruns
content:
Purpose / scope:
- Personal quick-docket for small, fast experiments: quant config sweeps + prompt variants + micro-evals. Not a polished lab notebook — dump of ideas, run notes, and TODOs so I don’t lose momentum between meetings.

Today’s high-level hypothesis:
- Q1: Q5-like 5-bit quant with asymmetric scales (per-channel) should preserve end-task coherence for summarization prompts but may degrade instruction-following when prompts include nested system messages.
- Q2: Lightweight prefix caching (100-token LRU) will reduce latency variance for short interactive chats but may introduce stale KV issues when rollout changes tokenizer or prompt templates.

Quick run summary (chronological):
- 2026-03-11 09:20 — baseline: fp16, model: open-vicuna-13b-v2 (pull from model-catalog tag v2.1). Test set: 120 summarization seeds (news-paragraphs). Metric: ROUGE-L, median latency (cold). Results: ROUGE-L=0.44, median latency=67ms/token, peak mem=12.8GB.
- 2026-03-11 10:05 — q5b per-channel (8 groups), no KV cache. Same seed. ROUGE-L=0.42 (drop ~4.5%), median latency=45ms/token, peak mem=5.4GB. Notes: some truncation on long outputs (~2% of cases).
- 2026-03-11 11:00 — q5b + activation folding enabled (runtime flag: --act-fold). ROUGE-L=0.421, median latency=40ms/token, mem=5.0GB. Activation folding helps tail latency slightly.
- 2026-03-11 14:30 — q4h (symmetric per-tensor) quick check. ROUGE-L=0.39, compression artifacts in numericals (lists), mem=3.6GB. Decision: q4h too lossy for summarization.
- 2026-03-12 09:10 — prompt variant sweep for instruction-following (10 prompts x 50 seeds): baseline fp16 vs q5b. Observed that prompts with explicit nested system->assistant roles produce hallucination-like contradictions under q5b in ~6% of cases. Examples saved below.
- 2026-03-12 15:00 — KV cache prefixing test (LRU 100 tokens) in interactive chat mode. Baseline (no prefix) median P95 latency=210ms; with prefix median P95=140ms. However, observed two failure modes: (1) if prompt template updated mid-session, cached KV used stale tokens causing incorrect persona references; (2) when using mixed model variants (q5b fallback to fp16 during heavy load), cache format mismatch leads to explicit decode errors in 0.3% of requests. Filed INF-2412.

Representative failure examples (paste):
- seed 43, prompt: [system: "You are a travel assistant."] + user: "Plan a 2-day Kyoto itinerary."
  - fp16: coherent suggestions, temples + transit + timing.
  - q5b: includes a fabricated "Arishima Shrine" (non-existent) in slot 2. Context shows model confused with similar-sounding names in Japanese corpora.

- seed 17, nested system messages: system1: "Be concise." system2: "You must always ask clarifying Qs." user: "Summarize this article."
  - q5b: begins with long preamble, ignores second system directive. fp16 follows both.

Micro metrics to log (numbers for SRE/ops):
- q5b throughput (13b open-vicuna): 980 tokens/sec (batch=1, seq=512) on A10-equivalent; cost estimate ~0.38 USD per 1k tokens (rough).
- fp16 baseline throughput: 640 tokens/sec; cost estimate ~0.62 USD per 1k tokens.
- KV cache hit rate (interactive traces): 0.28 overall, improves to 0.51 when prefixing identical user context across sessions.

Runtime flags / configs used (copied for re-run):
- --model open-vicuna-13b-v2:v2.1 --precision q5b --per-channel-quant --groups 8 --act-fold true --kv-cache none
- interactive run: --kv-cache lru --kv-lru-size 100 --compat-check true
- fallback policy: route to fp16 if latency > 2x target for > 1 minute

Immediate notes / hypotheses to validate next:
1) Per-channel scaling seems to preserve token-level distributions for decoder attention heads better than per-tensor symmetric q4h — replicate on code-synthesis prompts to test hallucination sensitivity.
2) Activation folding + fused-gemm path may mitigate some tail-case instabilities; run longer 1k-seed test with diverse system prompts.
3) Cache format/versioning: need a lightweight format marker in cached blobs so runtime can invalidate across model-variant rollouts. Post to infra/kv-cache design doc.
4) Prompt-engineering mitigation: add explicit role-check in system message ("Enforce: follow both system directives, if conflicting ask clarifying Q") — test whether explicit instruction survives q5b quantization.

Planned experiments (next 48h):
- E1: 1k summarization seeds, compare fp16 / q5b / q5b+actfold. Track ROUGE, prompt-compliance score, latency distribution. Owner: Neel. ETA: 2026-03-15.
- E2: 500 instruction-follow seeds with nested-system prompts. Measure instruction-following drop delta. Owner: Samir. ETA: 2026-03-14.
- E3: KV cache format marker prototype in runtime (patch branch: pr/998). Smoke test for downgrade/fallback compatibility. Owner: Ava. ETA: 2026-03-16.

Short TODO (priority ordered):
- [ ] Push 1k summarization run to batch infra (ticket: INF-2418) — ensure GPU assignment consistent across runs.
- [ ] Add simple format-version header to KV cache blob (proto sketch in confluence).
- [ ] Export sample failing prompts and attach to JIRA INF-2412.
- [ ] Run ablation: q5b groups=4 vs groups=8 to find cost/quality sweet spot.
- [ ] Sync with Samir on prompt template changes (avoid mid-session edits until cache-versioning is live).

Notes to self / friction points:
- Running long batches on dedicated pools sometimes picks up different CUDA kernel versions; need to pin runtime image for reproducibility (logged in infra slack).
- Quick eval harness (local) tends to underreport tail latency vs hosted; always validate one sample run on dedicated.

Random ideas (brain dump):
- Could we do on-the-fly micro-quant: use q5b for all tokens except attention key/value for first 64 tokens in fp16 to preserve early-conditioning fidelity? Hardware cost higher but maybe small mem overhead. Worth one small test.
- Create a small "quant-sanity" eval set — 200 items across genres: code, math, conversation, instructions, world-knowledge. Run nightly and alert on >3% regression vs baseline.

Appendix: short run commands (for reproducibility)
- baseline: rcli run --model open-vicuna-13b-v2:v2.1 --precision fp16 --seq 512 --batch 1 --out results/baseline-20260311.json
- q5b: rcli run --model open-vicuna-13b-v2:v2.1 --precision q5b --quant-groups 8 --act-fold true --seq 512 --batch 1 --out results/q5b-20260311.json

End of docket.

If I don’t come back to this in a week: remind me to push E1 to nightly and sync with Ava on pr/998.
